ia_scan.tooth_tusk_passage: pp. 632-634: nail, claw, beak and tooth follow the logarithmic spiral; rodent incisors (beaver, Geomys) build a log spiral by summed anterior/posterior growth-rate differences; elephant tusk tip ~ coincides with the spiral pole; Mastodon angustidens low spiral angle vs mammoth high angle; very long tusks (mammoth, Babirussa) become curves of double curvature 'like a twisted horn'

primary_log_spiral.name: Mammuthus primigenius tusk (Museum Wiesbaden), Wikimedia Commons
primary_log_spiral.author: Ghedoghedo (Commons user)
primary_log_spiral.match_rationale: Thompson p. 634 names the mammoth tusk explicitly as the fully developed logarithmic-spiral tusk (elephant tusk 'growing gradually into the spiral tusk of the mammoth') and as a curve of double curvature. Dark-background museum photograph permits silhouette segmentation of centreline + taper.

primary_torsion.name: Narwhal (Monodon monoceros) ivory tusk close-up showing sinistral spiral grooves, Wikimedia Commons (Flickr, CC BY 2.0)
primary_torsion.match_rationale: Thompson's 1917 Ch. XIII text never names the narwhal (grep of the IA full text: 0 hits); his torsion argument is made on Ovis ammon horns and extended to long tusks (mammoth, Babirussa) only as 'curves of double curvature'. The narwhal tusk is the canonical twisted tooth and the only tusk with a published angular dataset (Kiladze & Chernova 2018), so it is used here as a labelled analogue to test the torsion/helix component; it is NOT Thompson's own specimen.

planned_tests: T1 log-spiral vs circle (constant-curvature) fit of the segmented mammoth-tusk centreline about a fitted pole (Pearson r of ln r vs theta, RMSE, KS test on residuals)
T2 Thompson accretion law kappa(s) * w(s) = const (differential growth across a gnomonically widening section) vs kappa(s) = const null, via coefficient of variation along the tusk

T3 narwhal groove helix angle by structure-tensor orientation vs Kiladze & Chernova (2018) alpha = 66.88 +/- 0.61 deg; St Venant uniform-twist prediction tan(phi) proportional to local radius tested along the tusk
T4 St Venant equilateral-prism warping function reproduced and compared with Thompson Fig. 321 (six alternating sign sectors; one sign change per face)
